name: GS_Route
returns: int gate slot of the start sector to take | -1 already there | -2 no route
summary: Returns which gate of sector (x1,y1) leads on the best route to sector (x2,y2) on the galaxy route map.
semantics: Works on the universe route map (24 x 20 sectors, index x*20+y, 6 gate slots each, filled by GS_AddGate / the universe file). Fast form: argc == 6 and neither pos1 nor pos2 is an array: Nav::UniverseBuildRouteTable (a cached per-target shortest-path table by jumps, built on demand, invalidated by any gate change) answers the exit gate of the source, -1 when source == target, -2 when unreachable. Otherwise A* (Nav::UniverseFindRouteAStar) from position pos1 {x,y,z} in (x1,y1) to pos2 in (x2,y2) (a non-array position counts as 0,0,0; array elements are read without a size check): edge cost = gate-to-gate km times the weight of the sector owner's race. Weights: argc < 7 -> all 1; weights is an array -> element i per race (index = sector owner), missing or 0 entries take element 0 (itself 1 when 0 or > 0xffff); weights is an int -> a race bit mask: bit set 155, clear 100 (so races in the mask are avoided). The A* answer is the gate slot to take from the start sector, -1 if start == target, -2 if no route. Synchronous, no world change.
fl: differs: FL has 31 race weights (bits 0..30 of the mask) instead of 20
bugs: AP Nav::GsRouteCommand 0x00418b80: array results of Script::ArrayGetElement are dereferenced without a NULL check (0x00418bf4 and 8 more): a position or weights array shorter than read (e.g. pos with < 3 elements) reads address 1 -> crash. A sector owner >= 20 (GS_SetSectorOwner without check, or owner 0xffff after GS_RemoveGate of slot 6, B26) indexes the 20-entry weight array on the stack out of range. x3_src reproduces both (bugs.md audit list / B26).
notes: The position scale inside the A* (pos units vs gate positions /500000) was not verified.

name: GS_RouteDist
summary: Returns the length in km of the best gate route from a position in sector (x1,y1) to a position in (x2,y2).
semantics: Always the A* path (no fast table form, even with 6 args and no positions): same arguments, positions and race weights as GS_Route. Answers the route length in km (truncated gate-to-gate and position-to-gate distances summed, unweighted), the straight in-sector distance when start == target, or -1 when there is no route.
bugs: Same as GS_Route: unchecked ArrayGetElement results (crash on short arrays) and unchecked race index into the weight array (AP 0x00418b80); reproduced in x3_src.

name: GS_RouteLen
returns: int number of jumps | -2 (fast form, unreachable) | -1 (A* form, no route)
summary: Returns the number of gate jumps on the route from sector (x1,y1) to sector (x2,y2).
semantics: Fast form (argc == 6 and no position arrays): Nav::UniverseGetRouteHop: the hop count from the cached route table (built on demand); -2 if unreachable (0 for the same sector). Otherwise the A* path as GS_Route and the answer is the jump count of the found route, or -1 if none. Note the different not-found values of the two forms.
bugs: Same unchecked array/race index issues as GS_Route (AP 0x00418b80), reproduced in x3_src.

name: GS_SetSectorOwner
summary: Sets the owner race of sector (x,y) on the route map (used for the race weights of GS_Route*).
semantics: UniverseMap.sectors[x*20+y].owner = (ushort)race; answers 0. The route table is not invalidated (the owner only affects A* costs). No range check of x, y or race.
bugs: AP 0x00418bb5..0x00418bc0: x, y are not range-checked - out-of-range values write a word anywhere relative to the map; a race >= 20 (FL >= 31) later makes the A* read past its weight array. Reproduced in x3_src (bugs.md audit list, Nav::GsRouteCommand).

name: GS_AddGate
summary: Puts gate slot gate of sector (x,y) on the route map, leading to gate gate2 of sector (x2,y2), at position pos.
semantics: Nav::UniverseSetGate(slot=gate, destGate=gate2, x, y, x2, y2, pos/500000 per axis). Both gate numbers are accepted when unsigned <= 6, else nothing is written. Slot 0..5: the slot's destination row/col (stored as bytes), destination gate (word) and position are set. Then the sector's smallest gate distance is recomputed and the whole route table invalidated (rebuilt on the next query). Answers 0 in every case. pos elements are read without a size/type check. KC WarpGate.AddTo/SetPos use it.
bugs: B26 (bugs.md, open): slot/gate checks are 'CMP 6; JA' so slot 6 is accepted although only 0..5 exist: AP 0x00417b20 writes over the sector header (min gate distance, owner word, A* fields) and the gate never routes. x3_src reproduces it on purpose (writeLegacySeventhGate). Also pos shorter than 3 -> NULL element read (crash), reproduced.

name: GS_RemoveGate
summary: Removes gate slot gate of sector (x,y) from the route map.
semantics: Nav::UniverseClearGate(slot=gate, x, y): slot unsigned <= 6 accepted (else nothing): the slot gets destination -1/-1, gate -1, position 0; the sector's min gate distance is recomputed and the route table invalidated. Answers 0. KC WarpGate.Destruct uses it.
bugs: B26 (bugs.md, open): slot 6 is accepted (AP 0x00417bf1 'CMP EDX,6; JA'); it writes the sector header: owner becomes 0xffff, so a later GS_Route* A* reads weights[65535] past its stack array. Reproduced in x3_src.
